evals.name: edit-history-triage
evals.prompt: I'm in the cc-session-tool repo (the current working directory). I think the last Claude Code session that edited index.ts on the main branch may have introduced a regression. Find that session and report: (a) the session UUID, (b) the tools it ran before the first edit/write, and (c) a one-paragraph summary of the assistant's reasoning around the first edit. Return raw findings, no need to fix anything.
evals.expected_output: Identifies a specific session UUID, lists tool calls from turns before first_edit_turn, and shows assistant thinking/text near that turn. Uses cc-session-tool list/shape/tools/messages rather than reading JSONL files directly.

evals.name: subagent-investigation
evals.prompt: I want to audit the subagents from the most recent Claude Code session in this project (the current working directory) that spawned any. Tell me which session that is (its UUID), then for each subagent tell me: its agent_id, what it was asked to do, how many tool calls it made, and whether any of its tool calls errored. Don't fix anything — just report.
evals.expected_output: Finds the most recent session in the project with subagent_count > 0 (e.g., via list --include-subagents) and reports its UUID. Lists every subagent of that session, with agent_id, description, tool count, and a flag for whether any tool errored. Uses subagents + tools/shape with colon notation (<session>:<agent-id>), not direct file reads.

evals.name: bash-test-audit
evals.prompt: I'm in the cc-session-tool repo (the current working directory). Over the last 30 days, how often have I run `bun test` from Claude Code in this project? I want a total count, a per-session breakdown for the top 3 sessions by count, and a rough day-by-day distribution. Don't include sessions from other projects.
evals.expected_output: Reports a total count, the top 3 sessions by count, and a day-by-day distribution, scoped to this project (no --all-projects) and the last 30 days. Uses cc-session-tool search with --tool Bash --input-match 'bun test' --aggregate count-per-session for per-session counts and --tool Bash --aggregate counters --counter tests='bun test' --bucket day for the distribution (not --bash, which these aggregations don't count). States that the counts are Bash calls whose command contains `bun test` rather than individual test runs, and that the 30-day window and day buckets use each session's start date.
